x: Mel Thorpe (Warwickshire)

Trevor Hart and Mel Thorpe joined Gerry to make up a team and finished 74th and 150th respectively; placing Belgrave 18th. Trevor's run was probably his best to date, and there were many notable runners behind him.

Gerry North,Batty and Price went straight to the front,and Mel Thorpe and John Moore were soon dogging their heels. Half-way round the 10miles 700yd course Gerry just led from the Thurrock man,with the remainder well down.
In the Shaftsbury'10' on August 8th,Mel Thorpe finished 16th in a field of 139 competitors and clocked a useful 52:55.
Mel Thorpe had the difficult job of staying with D. Cooke and was unequal to the task, by 31 seconds.
Mel Thorpe,running in Belgrave colours for the first time on the Brighton road,was faced with the problem of dealing with Reynolds of Portsmouth and John Snowden of Surrey.

Mel Thorpe backed up well in 40th position after a period in the middle of the race when he had an attack of stitch. Most of the Belgrave contingent of 14(our best ever turn-out in this race)were satisfied with their runs.

The star studded cast threw everything into the performance: Mel Thorpe(Pyramus) and Brian Nott (Thisbe) made as fine a pair of lovers as ever graced the stage of the Old Vic and the supporting players,Ted Stimpson (Moonshine), Alan Mead (Wall),Howerd Satchell (Lion)and Chris Steer (producer,directo…

We had two "first timers" in the Midland event - Geoff North and Mel Thorpe. Both were previously Lancashire thro' residence,but since moving South decided to adopt their County of birth - Warwickshire.

At halfway Geoff and Tony were still pushing the pace with Mel Thorpe hanging on extremely well. Black and O'Hara were dropping and the defending champion, Dabbs, did not look his usual self but was managing to hold his 5th place.
Mel Thorpe had a great race finishing 5th,and the ever-present Charlie Walker completed our scoring team in 22nd place. John Moore,Ken Stimpson and John Baker also enjoyed an outing.
The revival commenced on Stage 6 with Mel Thorpe. Displaying scintillating form he scorched round the lap to take nearly a minute off the Cambridge man and move us up to 5th place.
John Thresher took the first leg for the A team with Mel Thorpe running for the B team. John gained a ten seconds lead over Manchester & District Lads Club with Mel third about 200 yards behind.

Jack reduced this lead to 22 seconds and sent off Mel Thorpe with every chance of going into the lead. Mel made no mistake, and producing almost the carbon copy of an earlier race when Laurie O'Hara took this stage, came home with fifteen seconds to spare.

Mel Thorpe (in great form these days) was second in 4:19.8 and Bill Kerr third in 4:20.2. The 3000m Steeplechase (a new championship event which should become more popular) proved an easy victory for John Bicourt whose experience at this type of race was too much for John Dear who had led in the early stages .

Some really hard work was put in by John Thresher in the 'half' and in stopping the watches at 1:54.9 he made some amends for his defeat in the Club Champs by 'you know who' . Other noteworthy times were Mel Thorpe's 4:16.2 in the mile (best for some years) and John Dear's 4:25.0 (best ever).
He burst away from the field,which included our own Mel Thorpe,and really looked most impressive. Unfortunately he could only keep it up for a few laps before the bunch caught him again.
The race for the minor positions was a different kettle of fish though,Barry Collins and Bob Holt just managing to get away from Mel Thorpe in the latter stages.
Mel Thorpe (9:08.6) was the individual winner with Laurie O'Hara (9:17:0) 4th and Tony Fairclough (9:18:0) 5th. Our score of 10 points was too good for Woodford Green (20) and Kent (22).
Mel Thorpe ran soundly to anchor our 'B' team in 12th place. Hercules, in not only finishing first but breaking the record, proved the benefit of solid team running.

Walton cut our lead to 1minute 11 secs on the fifth stage, moving into 2nd place, but Charlie Dabbs had done enough to hand Mel Thorpe a comfortable lead which he increased, bringing us home 1 minute 17 secs ahead of Walton AC.

Pat Newell was next to run on the first of the short circuits (3½ miles) and soon overtook the Portsmouth runner (Plumpton) but Reading and Windsor were soon upon him and Pat had to be content to hand over to Mel Thorpe in 4th place.

Mel Thorpe gave a good account of himself with a first class effort which took us up to 4th. Ahead, however, Dick Taylor of Coventry was building up a good lead by dropping Dave Cooke of Portsmouth,who in turn took his team away from Bristol.
(rear)Charlie Dabbs, Charlie Smart,Trevor Hart,Ron Mitchell,Arthur Bruce,Howard Satchell,Ron Linstead,Mel Thorpe,John Thresher.

All the 'A' team (Mel Thorpe, Laurie O'Hara, Trevor Hart and Tony Fairclough) ran well in a very classy field. Chris Steer, the new Club 20 mile Champion, had to be content with leading our 'B' team home on this occasion.

Mel Thorpe became the 7th Belgravian in 20 years to take the individual silver medal in this year's South of Thames "Junior" Race. He therefore follows in the footsteps of those other runners-up, Denis Main, Len Marchant Charlie Walker, Pat Newell, Pete Bagnall, and George Flanagan.

Adrian Major and Chris Steer both made up two places but by this time the first two clubs (Windsor and Reading) were well ahead and it was left to John Bicourt and Mel Thorpe to maintain 3rd position, although Mel was closing fast on Reading towards the end.
The two Norths then took well over a minute off Drewett and Badgery of Mitcham leaving Mel Thorpe to thoroughly enjoy himself by putting a further 350 yards between us and our rivals.
Mel Thorpe and Chris Steer were a further 13 secs and 26 secs further back respectively and Trevor Hart, with a little more in hand than usual, our fourth scorer.

Belgrave looked set for second after good runs by Laurie O'Hara and Mel Thorpe, but Bob Holt(Herc) squeezed in front of Tony Fairclough on the penultimate leg and Chris Steer was passed by Collins (Windsor) on the last.

Mel Thorpe had a great run. Forcing the pace for most of the race he had to give way at the line to the fast-finishing Church (Walton)---it was of little consolation to see his rival on his knees a little afterwards or to know that another lap would probably have "burnt them off".
Mel Thorpe suffered a little and fell to 72nd compared to his 40th position last year. That stalwart of the long distance section, Philip King, completed our team in 267th place.

… the handicap - form that suggests he will be running yet again for Belgrave in the Southern Championships in February. Mel Thorpe, recent runner-up in the South of Thames Junior, took 2nd handicap prize and John Dear 3rd.…
In 2½ years Mel Thorpe has raised himself from a very unfit athlete to a runner who is virtually an automatic selection for our Championship teams.
Mel Thorpe and John Bicourt were fairly well placed but with the exception of Adrian in the early 50's, we were having to wait too long for our other scoring men.

Held on the same day as the Inter-Counties Championship at Blackpool, this third league match found us with our points lead in jeopardy, as Gerry and Geoff North, John Thresher, Tony Fairclough and Trevor Hart were on call by their Counties and Mel Thorpe, Alan Black, and John Dear were also away.

Over the last lap our fortunes wavered for Mel Thorpe,who had been running very well, dropped back twelve places,but Laurie O'Hara who had been late arriving and started without a warm-up, was coming through fast and gained fourteen positions to pass both Thorpe and Dabbs.

Mel Thorpe had great difficulty in getting to the start on time. A fast car drive from Blackburn and a sprint from the dressing-room enabled him to just make it, but this, together with the effects of his present move to Coventry must have left him with precious little nervous energy for an event of this stature.

Charlie Dabbs turned in another of his fine performances to take 18th place while, with Mel Thorpe kept out of the race because of 'flu', a private battle ensued further down the field between Chris Keavey and Gordon Biscoe to decide who should complete the scoring three.

In spite of this Laurie O'Hara and Mel Thorpe ran extremely well to take 5th and 20th places respectively in a very strong field. It was good to see Eric Penny back in action again and we hope to see more of him on the road.

The result augured well for the Johnstone Relay the following week at Hornchurch, for to supplement our heroes of Blackheath we had Gerry North, Joe Reilly, Laurie O'Hara, Mel Thorpe, Trevor Hart and Charlie Dabbs, with Fairclough and Black withdrawing.
With two laps of the "top" completed the leader's margin was 60 yards, and at this point Mel Thorpe left Dabbs and Reilly to cut into Trevor's lead with a gusto that promised great things.
Left; Charlie Dabbs gives Trevor Hart a 32 seconds lead Right: John Thresher takes over from Mel Thorpe. STAGE 4: John Bicourt (15:48 - 2nd fastest)
However, with Bill Dance 'on form' and Chris Steer running through to chase Mel Thorpe home in the last mile, the team closed in worthy winners of the race.

It was at 3-15 pm that Bill Lucas sent over 300 runners on their way over the 5 mile course at Sparrows Den, West Wickham, and it was with some suprise that after a small lap of 1 mile Brian Buxton was seen to be leading the field followed closely by Bill Dance, Mel Thorpe, Adrian Major and John Dear.
Mel Thorpe also appeared and placed 24th, 2mins 31secs. behind Geoff. Unfortunately, further illness prevented Geoff from competing at Leicester.

To hope to hang on to Mel Thorpe indefinately when he now lives as distant as Coventry was too good to be true. Perhaps it might have been different if it were not such a struggle to make the team these days.
